name: Ironpass Former Combat Medic Bartender's Shift Set
description: Dark utility trousers with medical-kit loop webbing still sewn into the left thigh, now holding a bottle opener and a rag instead of trauma shears. A plain olive henley with the sleeves always rolled precisely to the elbow — a habit from sterile procedure — revealing a forearm with two mismatched chrome fingers on the left hand. A low-profile apron in black canvas, front-pocketed, worn with the same economy of movement as body armor.
functionality: Medical loop webbing repurposed for bar tools; chrome fingers provide non-slip grip on glassware in any weather.
what_it_says: Someone who has seen worse than anything this bar will throw at them, and is quietly fine with that.
manufacturer: Ironpass (trousers base); apron sourced locally; chrome from Vansen AugMount
story_hooks: The medical webbing loops are from a specific theater of conflict — a regular at the bar served in the same unit and hasn't said anything yet.
Someone comes in tonight with a wound that needs immediate attention, and the bartender's hands remember exactly what to do.

physical_description.visual_profile: A utilitarian silhouette built from repurposed military-medical gear, worn with the precise, economical posture of someone trained to move efficiently in high-stress environments. The overall impression is one of controlled competence—no excess, no flourish, every element serving a function. The rolled sleeves expose augmentation, signaling both capability and a deliberate choice not to hide it.
physical_description.fit: Slim, tapered trousers with a high waist for stability; henley fitted but not tight through the chest and shoulders to allow unrestricted arm movement; apron sits low on the hips, doesn't interfere with torso rotation.
physical_description.primary_material: Ironpass ballistic-weave trousers (reinforced Cordura composite); standard cotton-poly blend henley; black canvas apron with ripstop reinforcement at stress points.
physical_description.texture: Trousers have a subtle grip texture from their original combat coating, now worn smooth at the knees and thighs. Henley is soft from repeated washing but retains a slight stiffness along the seams. Apron canvas is broken-in, with a soft nap but structured enough to hold its shape when loaded.
physical_description.color_scheme: Charcoal-gray trousers with OD green webbing; olive henley; matte black canvas apron. The chrome augmentation on the left forearm provides a cool metallic accent against warm skin tone.
physical_description.closures: Trousers: traditional button fly with reinforced stitching. Henley: pullover, no closure. Apron: heavy-duty D-ring adjustment at the back, allows quick on/off.
distinctive_features: Medical-kit loop webbing still stitched into left thigh—now repurposed to hold a vintage steel bottle opener and a bleached cotton rag
Henley sleeves always rolled to the elbow in a precise, practiced fold—the crease holds even after washing
Left forearm featuring two mismatched chrome fingers: older, matte-gray surgical-grade on index; newer, polished titanium-alloy on ring finger, suggesting incremental augmentation over years
Apron front pockets designed to hold glassware without shifting; rear reinforcement for carrying full drink trays
Faded stress marks on trousers at hip flexors and thigh where medical gear used to mount
Slight discoloration on the henley's left shoulder—old blood stain that won't fully wash out, now a ghost of the wearer's former life
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 3 functional, bordering Tier 4. The base garments are quality working-class (Ironpass is mid-market), but they're heavily worn and repurposed. The chrome augmentation is modest—surgical-grade, not flashy—suggesting practical enhancement over status.
physical_description.cultural_context: Signals a former military-medical background (combat medic) now civilian-employed in the service industry. The visible augmentation and utilitarian aesthetic broadcast competence and a refusal to code-switch. Wearing this outfit says: 'I know how to work under pressure, I've saved lives, and now I'm building a different kind of livelihood. Take me as I am.'
physical_description.condition_typical: Broken-in but maintained. Trousers are creased where they fold, fabric slightly faded at the seams from repeated wear and laundering. Apron shows scuffs and faint stains (lime juice, bitters, old coffee) that don't fully come out. The henley is soft, possibly re-dyed once or twice to keep it looking intentional rather than threadbare. The chrome fingers are clean and functional—they receive regular maintenance. Nothing is torn or actively falling apart, but nothing is new either.

image_prompt: A former combat medic working the bar shift, shot in moody golden-amber neon light from overhead. Dark-skinned model with a calm, focused expression, standing three-quarter to camera, left arm extended slightly to show the mismatched chrome fingers catching the light—one dull surgical gray, one polished titanium. Charcoal trousers crisp at the thigh where the medical webbing is visible, holding a vintage bottle opener. Olive henley with sleeves precisely rolled to the elbows, no wrinkles. Black canvas apron worn low, front pockets shadowed and deep. Background: a GLMZ dive bar interior, blurred bottles on shelves, wet counter surface reflecting neon. Mood: quiet competence, no wasted movement. Shot from a distance that captures the full utilitarian silhouette against a dark brick wall with faint holographic ad interference. --ar 2:3 --v 6
